findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed IO error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, AuditIoError> and use map_err or ? to propagate io::Error as a domain audit error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value fields
findings.failure_mode: malformed audit data (e.g. a string value) causes a panic instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use map_err on the parse result to return a domain ParseError, and propagate through the function Result

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing into a Vec that may be empty or short
findings.failure_mode: a blank line or line with zero commas produces a Vec with length 1, causing index 0 to panic if the line is empty; or a line with no comma produces parts[1] panic on line 13
findings.fix: use get(0) and check Some, or destructure with split_once(',') and pattern match on the two expected parts

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing into a Vec that may have fewer than 2 elements
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one comma-separated field (or no comma) causes an index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: use get(1) with check, or restructure with split_once(',') and match on the (name, value) tuple

findings.problem: as u16 after parse::<u32>() is a lossy cast that silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value in range 65536..=4294967295 silently wraps to a wrong u16 value, corrupting audit data without any error indication
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap_or_else(|_| u32::MAX)) or better: parse directly via u16::from_str_radix or use checked_into::<u16>() and map_err on None

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) couples logging/I/O into the data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: side effects embedded in a function that should be a pure boundary parser make the function untestable in isolation and couples the shell to the core
findings.fix: remove println! from load_audits; logging should be performed by the caller (imperative shell) after the pure core returns

findings.problem: collects every split field into Vec<String> before consuming index 0 and 1
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations and clones for every line; for large audit files this adds measurable memory pressure and GC cost
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get (name, rest), then trim and parse rest; avoid Vec<String> allocation entirely

findings.problem: load_audits returns Vec<Record> directly instead of Result<Vec<Record>, E>
findings.failure_mode: all failure modes (IO error, parse error, malformed line) are hidden behind panics with no typed error contract exposed to callers
findings.fix: define an AuditError enum (IoError, ParseError, MalformedLine) and return Result<Vec<Record>, AuditError>

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_audits throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler evidence for CPU hotspot characterization of the parsing loop
no allocation audit (e.g., criterion with measurement_type=Allocs or heaptrack) for Vec<String> per-line overhead
no second-ring evidence (assembly or MIR) showing bounds-check elimination on parts[0] / parts[1] access patterns
no command-evidence gate output (cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy) for this crate
residual_risk: static review only with no commands run; 5 BLOCKER findings for unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy cast, and missing error propagation in a single-file crate that processes untrusted file input. All panics are reachable from external data and constitute denial-of-service vectors. The crate must be repaired to return Result with typed errors, eliminate all unwrap/index, and use checked conversions before it can be considered safe.
